Early''' (born April 17, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Zamalek SC Basketball|Zamalek]] of the [[Egyptian Basketball Premier League]]. He was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] college player at [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State University]] after a stint at [[Sullivan County Community College]], and was drafted in the second round of the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]]. ==Early life== Early was born in [[the Bronx]].{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Suellentrop|title=Going to Knicks 'a blessing' for Cleanthony Early|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article1147571.html|access-date=June 30, 2014|work=Kansas.com|date=June 30, 2014}} After Early's cousin was murdered, his mother decided to leave the city and relocate to suburban [[Middletown, Orange County, New York|Middletown, New York]] when he was 14. Early attended [[Pine Bush High School]] in [[Pine Bush, New York]] before transferring to [[Mount Zion Christian Academy]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]]. Tragedy affected Early once again after his brother drowned in [[Schoharie Creek]] at age 32. This led to Early wanting to be closer to his family and attending [[Sullivan County Community College]].{{cite web|first=Jonah|last=Ballow|title=Overcoming Tragedy, Cleanthony Early Returns to Big Apple|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/overcoming-tragedy-cleanthony-early-returns-big-apple|access-date=July 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2014}} As a high school junior, Early told the ''[[Times Herald-Record]]'' that he was only {{height|ft=6|in=5}} tall despite being listed at {{height|ft=6|in=6}}.{{cite news |last=Witt |first=Kevin |title=Hello There, Cleanthony Early |url=https://www.recordonline.com/article/20090103/sports31/901030332 |access-date=November 16, 2020 |work=[[Times Herald-Record]] |date=January 3, 2009 |language=en}} Considered a two-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Early was listed as the No. 102 small forward in the nation in 2010.{{cite news|title=Cleanthony Early Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/99204/cleanthony-early|access-date=August 1, 2014|work=ESPN.com}} ==College career== Early was a [[junior college]] star at [[Sullivan County Community College]], where he was the two-time Division III [[NJCAA]] Player of the Year. After considering offers from major conference schools, he signed with [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] and coach [[Gregg Marshall]].{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Hurricane Irene helped Wichita State recruit Cleanthony Early | work = [[The Herald (Everett)|The Herald]] | date = April 6, 2013 | url = http://www.heraldnet.com/article/20130406/SPORTS/704069929 | access-date = November 25, 2013}} Early made an immediate impact for the Shockers, averaging 13.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 5.4 [[rebounds per game]]. He was named first team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference]] and the MVC Newcomer of the Year.{{cite web|last=Suellentrop|first=Paul|title=Wichita State's Cleanthony Early earns All-MVC honors|work=[[Wichita Eagle]]|date=October 30, 2013|url=http://www.kansas.com/2013/03/05/2702695/wichita-states-cleanthony-early.html|access-date=November 25, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203030711/http://www.kansas.com/2013/03/05/2702695/wichita-states-cleanthony-early.html|archive-date=December 3, 2013|url-status=dead}} In the post-season, Early led the team to the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 Final Four]] in [[Atlanta]]. In the Shockers' semifinal game against eventual champion [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], Early scored 24 points and collected 10 rebounds in a narrow 72–68 loss.{{cite news|title=Louisville edges upstart Wichita State, advances to NCAA title game|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330960097|access-date=April 6, 2013|work=ESPN.com|date=April 6, 2013}} He was named to the All-Final Four team for his efforts.{{cite web|title=MBB: Early Named Final Four All-Tournament|work=[[Wichita State Shockers]]|date=April 9, 2013|url=http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=207124060|access-date=November 25, 2013|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203104347/http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=207124060|url-status=dead}} Going into his senior season, Early gained widespread national attention. He was named preseason Player of the Year for the Missouri Valley Conference{{cite web | title = 2013–14 MVC Men's Basketball Preseason Team, Poll | work = [[Missouri Valley Conference]] | date = October 30, 2013 | url = http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2013-14/6914/2013-14-mvc-mens-basketball-preseason-team-poll/ | access-date = November 25, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131203001048/http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2013-14/6914/2013-14-mvc-mens-basketball-preseason-team-poll/ | archive-date = December 3, 2013 | url-status = dead }} and was named to the preseason top 50 watch lists for the [[John R. Wooden Award|John Wooden]]{{cite web | last = | first = | title = John R. Wooden Award Presented by Wendy's Reveals 2013–14 Preseason Top 50 | work = [[John Wooden Award]] | date = November 12, 2013 | url = http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1460 | access-date = November 25, 2013}} and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]] Awards for national player of the year.{{cite web|title=2013–2014 Men's 50-Player Watch List|work=[[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]]|date=|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1460|access-date = November 25, 2013}} Early helped lead the [[2013–14 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2013–14 team]] to an undefeated 34–0 record entering the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], becoming the first team in [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] men's basketball to do so [[1990–91 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|in over two decades]].{{cite news |url=http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/03/09/wichita-state-wins-mvc-ncaa-tournament-berth-fred-van-vleet/?eref=sihp |title=Wichita State reigns as MVC champions, finishes regular season at 34–0 |first=Michael |last=Beller |work=One and One |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 9, 2014 |access-date=March 9, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310022353/http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/03/09/wichita-state-wins-mvc-ncaa-tournament-berth-fred-van-vleet/?eref=sihp |archive-date=March 10, 2014 |url-status=dead }} Early put up an impressive effort in an attempt to help the Shockers advance to the Sweet Sixteen, with 31 points and 7 rebounds on 12-of-17 shooting. The Shockers ended up losing to [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] 78–76, ending their hopes of a Final Four repeat. ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2014–16)===
